source.title: A Simple yet Effective Baseline for Robust Deep Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Yucen Luo; Jun Zhu; Tomas Pfister

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains on datasets with varying fractions of corrupted labels and reports test performance, but it adds a variance regularizer and does not report whether training error reaches zero.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test errors under label corruption, but not training errors. Its discussion of real labels being learned before noisy labels cites prior work [2], so that is not extracted as a result. Figures showing test accuracy over epochs are not separately extracted where the tables give the relevant test errors.
record.test_reason: The study develops a mitigation for noisy-label overfitting and measures generalization, label-selection precision, and model complexity. It does not report training-label fit or separately measure learning of clean and corrupted labels. Its own results therefore do not establish any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their variance-based regularizer reduces overfitting and improves generalization under corrupted labels, including severe noise. They also present a Jacobian-norm interpretation and lower measured model complexity; they do not establish perfect fitting of corrupted training labels.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments add a predictive-variance regularizer to supervised training; CIFAR experiments use WRN-28-10 and ImageNet uses ResNet-50. The study does not test the unmodified recipe on completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance as the label-noise ratio varies and says performance is stable across a wide range of regularizer values λ.

fits_no_version.finding: With variance regularization, CIFAR-10 test error rises from 3.79% at zero corruption to 13.31% at 80% uniform corruption; CIFAR-100 rises from 18.6% to 44.68%. Training error is not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization degrades as uniform label corruption increases under the proposed variance-regularized training procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1–4 show baseline test accuracy deteriorating later in training, while variance regularization reduces this deterioration. Figure 3 reports higher clean-label precision among examples selected by low training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variance regularization reduces late-training generalization deterioration and improves the precision of low-loss example selection under label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 5–6 report lower local intrinsic dimensionality and critical sample ratio with the proposed regularizer on CIFAR-10 with 60% uniform noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variance regularization yields lower measured representation dimensionality and decision-boundary complexity in this noisy-label setting.

record.problems: Training error is not reported for the noisy-label experiments, so the results cannot establish whether the models fit the corrupted training labels perfectly. The proposed method includes an added regularizer, and the reported corruption fractions do not reach 100%.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the test-error results do not by themselves measure the perfect training-set fit required by V4, and no other version's specified behavior is tested.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters; experiments stop at 80% uniform corruption and report no training error.
Time required to fit true versus random labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Training-set fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fit throughout the corruption range and degradation toward chance at complete corruption. Test-error increases are reported, but without training-fit measurements or a complete-corruption endpoint.

Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization. The added variance regularizer does not test these propositions.

Direct comparison of when shared clean patterns and noisy labels are learned. Test-accuracy trajectories and label-selection precision do not establish this learning order; the explicit clean-first claim is attributed to prior work.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to uses_without_test/T4. The absence of training-fit measurements prevents treating the test-error tables as evidence for the joint fitting-and-generalization claim in V4. No existing rows require correction, and no omitted result directly measures a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: No result establishes zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels without changing the model or hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time for fitting true versus random labels or across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
Test errors are reported across corruption fractions, but training-set fit is not reported; the paper's method adds variance regularization.
No tests of whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether their removal harms clean-label generalization.
The paper cites prior work on early pattern learning and later noisy-label memorization but does not test that learning order.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
